```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4.5, out.width = "100%")
has_tskit <- malariafwd::tskit_available()
has_gg <- requireNamespace("ggplot2", quietly = TRUE)
## the build machine's temporary directory, shown as <tempdir>: a run's printed directory is the
## reader's own, not the machine's that built this page
local({
  td <- tempdir(); out <- knitr::knit_hooks$get("output")
  knitr::knit_hooks$set(output = function(x, options) out(gsub(td, "<tempdir>", x, fixed = TRUE), options))
})
```

A single `malariafwd` run writes a handful of files into its output directory. This
vignette tours them — what each output means and how to explore it. It reads
`example_run()`, a run that ships with the package: 60 hosts and 150 mosquitoes for 400 days,
with imports, case management, recrudescence and co-transmission (several genotypes in a bite)
switched on, so that every kind of case occurs.
The chunks that read the tree sequence need Python with tskit (see `check_setup()`).

## Run one simulation

With SLiM, a run of your own is one call (not run here):

```{r, eval = FALSE}
p   <- vivax_params(N_HOSTS = 100, N_MOSQ = 250, BITING_RATE = 0.1, SIM_DAYS = 548)
run <- run_sim(p, seed = 1, outdir = file.path(tempdir(), "anatomy"))   # a few seconds on a laptop
```

Here, the bundled run:

```{r}
library(malariafwd)
run <- example_run()
dir(run$outdir)
```

`run` points at the output directory, which holds:

- `events.tsv` — every discrete event (infections, clearances, relapses, mosquito uptake …)
- `state.tsv` — per-tick state of every host and mosquito
- `plasmo.trees` — the tskit tree sequence (the genealogy behind IBD)
- `params.tsv`, `cmdline.txt`, `model.slim`, `run.log` — provenance of the run
- `DONE` — written last: when the run finished, a key of its parameters and seed, and the size of
  every file, so a directory that is not a whole run can be told from one that is

`?events.tsv` and `?state.tsv` describe every column.

## The event log

Every row of `events.tsv` carries an `event_type`. `event_types()` is the dictionary:

```{r}
event_types()

ev <- load_events(run)                 # a data.table
ev[, .N, by = event_type][order(-N)]   # how many of each event type
```

Classify each blood-stage clone onset ("case") by its true origin: one row per clone, and the
clones that became patent in one host on one day share an `episode_id`. There are **four** origins: `relapse`
(a hypnozoite activated), `imported`, `local reinfection`, and `recrudescence` (a clone that
survived a treatment course, was suppressed below patency, and re-expanded). The fourth only
appears when treatment can fail *and* `P_RECRUD_GIVEN_FAIL > 0`. At the shipped defaults there is
no treatment at all, so a default run shows three; the example run has case management with
recrudescence on, so it shows all four:

```{r}
cs <- classify_cases(ev)
cs[, .N, by = origin]
```

Every episode of a host after its first is a recurrence. `recurrences()` pairs each with the
host's earlier episodes, with both sides' true origins; `episodes()` gives every clone's span.

```{r}
rec <- recurrences(ev)
rec[, .N, by = .(origin, prior_origin)]
```

## Epidemiology over time

`summarise_run()` gives prevalence, the complexity of infection (COI, the distinct lineages in an
infected host), the entomological inoculation rate (EIR), the force of infection from bites and
imports (FOI) and the molecular force of blood-stage infection, which adds the relapses (molFOB):

```{r}
summarise_run(run)     # over the second half of the run
fo <- force_of_infection(run, split_imported = FALSE)
fo[win %in% c(0, 180, 390), .(win, origin, n)]   # new cases in three 30-day windows, by origin
```

## Who infected whom

Every local infection has a true infector: the genome a mosquito took up before the bite. A bite can
also leave hypnozoites, so a link runs to each relapse the bite causes later, often months on.

```{r}
links <- transmission_links(ev)
links[, .(infected = sum(weight)), by = kind]     # through a bite's blood stage, or a relapse
rc_by_origin(run, from = 100, followup = 100)    # secondary cases per case, by true origin
```

## A single host's trajectory

`state.tsv` records every host each tick. Take the host with the most relapses and plot its
blood-stage clones, a colour for each lineage, and its dormant hypnozoites through time:

```{r, eval = has_gg}
st <- load_state(run)      # each host's state, day by day
h  <- ev[event_type == "hypnozoite_activation", .N, by = human_id][order(-N), human_id[1]]
plot_host_trajectory(run, host_id = h)
```

Hosts by state over time: uninfected, patent without or with hypnozoites, subpatent only, and
hypnozoites only:

```{r, eval = has_gg}
plot_host_state_prevalence(host_state_prevalence(st))
```

## The reservoir and relapses

The hypnozoite reservoir is the model's distinctive, otherwise-unobservable compartment:

```{r}
st <- load_state(run)
hs <- unique(host_state_prevalence(st)[, .(tick, hypnozoites_per_host)])
hs[tick %% 50 == 0]                          # mean hypnozoites per host, every 50 days
relapse_fraction(ev)                         # two readings, per episode and per acquisition: equal unless recrudescence is on
coi_distribution(st)                         # COI over the infected host-days: counts and shares
```

```{r, eval = has_gg}
plot_relapse_km(time_to_relapse(run))        # time to each batch's first relapse (Kaplan-Meier)
```

## Ground-truth relatedness

Because the full genealogy is recorded, identity-by-descent is exact rather than inferred:

```{r, eval = has_tskit}
rel <- ev[event_type == "hypnozoite_activation" & parent1_pedigree_id != -1]
x <- ibd_pairs(run, pairs = data.frame(a = rel$pedigree_id, b = rel$parent1_pedigree_id))
summary(ibd_lookup(x, rel$pedigree_id, rel$parent1_pedigree_id))   # each relapse vs its batch: IBD 1
```

Only the listed pairs are computed. To compare every pair among a set of genomes, pass `ids`
instead, which costs the square of their number.

The relatedness of the newly acquired infections follows transmission, quarter by quarter:

```{r, eval = has_tskit}
new_infection_diversity(run, bin = 90, cap = 40)   # mean IBD, clonal share and lineages, by quarter
```

## Seeing the relatedness, not just the number

`ibd_pairs()` gives one number per pair. `ibd_segments()` gives the stretches behind it, and
`plot_ibd_pair()` draws them along the chromosomes. Its `group` sets kinds of pair side by side:
a clonal pair (or a relapse against its origin) is shared end to end, same-oocyst siblings show
a recombination mosaic, unrelated genomes share nothing:

```{r, eval = has_tskit && has_gg, fig.height = 4.5}
tp <- ibd_truth_pairs(run)   # pairs whose true relationship the event log gives
show <- tp[cls %in% c("relapse vs its origin", "same-oocyst sibs", "distinct founders"),
           head(.SD, 2), by = cls]
plot_ibd_pair(run, show$a, show$b, group = show$cls)

# and the model-validation view: IBD by known relationship against the textbook rungs
plot_relatedness_ladder(tp)
```

## The ancestral recombination graph (ARG)

The model is neutral (mutation rate 0), so every *site* statistic is zero; tskit's **branch**
mode measures the genealogy directly. One caveat matters: the recorded genealogy is a
**forest** -- each founder lineage and each import is an independent root, so most pairs never
coalesce. Branch *divergence* therefore does not behave as a relatedness measure here; use
`arg_tmrca()`, which reports the time to the common ancestor together with `coalesced`, the
fraction of the genome over which one exists.

`tmrca` is a **depth** -- ticks from the older of the two genomes back to their shared
ancestor -- so a relapse and the hypnozoite it activated from give 0 no matter when in the run
they occurred. The raw tskit node time (ticks before the *end of the run*) is reported
separately as `tmrca_node_time`; it moves with sampling date rather than with relatedness.

```{r, eval = has_tskit}
rel <- ev[event_type == "hypnozoite_activation" & parent1_pedigree_id != -1][1]
arg_summary(run)                                   # trees, edges, roots/tree, oldest root
arg_tmrca(run, rel$pedigree_id, rel$parent1_pedigree_id)   # coalesced = 1, tmrca = 0
```

## Calibrating the uptake draws

`LAMBDA_OOCYSTS` / `LAMBDA_SPOROZOITES` are **pre-truncation** rates, so they are not the mean
counts a feeding study reports -- conditioning away the zeros pulls the realised mean up:

```{r}
uptake_moments(2)                      # Poisson lambda = 2 -> realised mean 2.31
uptake_moments(2, k = 1)               # overdispersed    -> realised mean 3.00
uptake_calibrate(mean = 2.5, var = 6)  # a target -> the lambda / K to set
```

## Repeating a run exactly

`SEED` is recorded as `ACTUAL_SEED` in `params.tsv`, alongside every resolved parameter, the derived
`GENOME_LENGTH` / `N_CHROMOSOMES` / `RECOMB_WITHIN`, and the SLiM and package versions
(`SLIM_VERSION`, `MALARIAFWD_VERSION`). Floats are recorded to 15 significant digits, the precision
`run_sim()` passes to SLiM. An extinct run's file ends with an `EXTINCT_TICK` row, and a run that
never started with a `NEVER_STARTED` row. `load_params()` reads the parameters back into the
`vivax_params()` set the run was made from, each of its type, so `run_sim(load_params(run), seed =
run$seed, outdir = ...)` repeats a run started from R exactly when each of its non-zero floats lies
between 1e-130 and 1e15 in magnitude: the same files, all but the tree sequence's provenance row,
where SLiM records when the run was made and the time and memory it took. The seed, the versions,
the derived genome and the outcome rows are on the `load_run()` object (`seed`, `slim_version`,
`malariafwd_version`, `genome_length`, `n_chromosomes`, `recomb_within`, `extinct_tick`,
`never_started`).

`DONE` records when the run finished, how long it took, its seed, a key of its parameters and seed
(the md5 of the arguments SLiM was given, without `OUTDIR` and `VERBOSE`), the md5 of the model, the
versions, and the size of every file; `load_run()` reports a directory whose `DONE` is missing or
whose files have changed since. SLiM runs in the run's directory on its copy of the model, so
running `slim` with the arguments in `cmdline.txt` from a directory holding `model.slim` repeats the
run.

Reproducing a run needs SLiM >= 5.2 on `PATH` and, for IBD and the ARG functions, Python with
`tskit` (>= 1.0) and `numpy` through reticulate; `check_setup()` reports both. `RETAIN_FULL_HISTORY
= T` is required for IBD to already-cleared infections -- without it, most earlier genomes leave the
tree, and `ibd_pairs()` warns about the ids it was asked for that are gone and gives them `NA`.

See the *Getting started* vignette for parameter sweeps with `run_grid()`, and
`?event_types` for the full event-type dictionary.
